title: Certificate of survey: initial survey
description: What to prepare to apply for a certificate of survey for a domestic commercial vessel and get it through its initial survey. Summarised from AMSA's guidance; AMSA's reply to your application lists the surveys your vessel actually needs.

sources.title: Survey frequency for domestic commercial vessels

items.title: Gather the vessel's details
items.detail: Type, measured length, breadth, depth, maximum design speed, hull material and the power (kW) of the largest engine.

items.title: Gather identity or organisation documents for the applicant
Engage an accredited marine surveyor
items.detail: Most vessels of 35 metres or more, and novel vessels, need a recognised organisation instead.

items.title: Apply to AMSA with Form 521
items.detail: The same form can cover a load line certificate if your vessel needs one.

items.title: Read AMSA's reply listing the surveys required
items.detail: Usually plan approval, construction and commissioning surveys for a new vessel.

items.title: Have the plans approved
items.detail: Your surveyor (or a naval architect) can tell you which plans and stability information are needed.

items.title: Pay AMSA's fee and wait for the outcome letter
Record the certificate and its expiry in your vessel's certificates
items.detail: A certificate of survey is normally valid for five years. AMSA sends a reminder 90 days before it expires.

items.title: Note when periodic surveys are due
items.detail: Depending on the vessel's survey frequency category (high, medium or low) there may be in-water or out-of-water surveys between the initial and renewal surveys.
